questions.stem: A 26-year patient having RBC count 2 lakhs/mm3, PCV 30%, and hemoglobin 9.3, what is the type of anemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Folic acid deficiency anemia
  • Hematocrit or Packed cell volume: Ratio of the volume of RBCs to Total volume of blood
  • Hct or PCV = MCV × RBC concentration

Now coming back to the question:

  • MCV =PCV/RBC count (in millions) = 30/0.2 = 150 (Increased)
  • MCH= Hb/RBC count = 9.3/ 0.2= 46 (Increased)
  • MCHC= Hb/ PCV= 31 (Normal)
  • Goes in favor of Macrocytic anemia, thus Option: B is correct.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 635, 636

questions.stemHtml: Identify the predominant abnormally shaped red cell type seen in the peripheral smear given below:
questions.solutionHtml:
Acanthocyte
  • Acanthocytes (Acanthos means spine) are cells of approximately spherical shape bearing between 2 and 20 spicules that are of unequal length and distributed irregularly over the red cell surface. Some of the spicules have club-shaped rather than pointed ends.


Dacie & Lewis NCEHaematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 74

Liver disease
  • Acanthocytes (Acanthos means spine) aka Spur cells are cells of approximately spherical shape bearing between 2 and 20 spicules that are of unequal length and distributed irregularly over the red cell surface. Some of the spicules have club-shaped rather than pointed ends.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 74

questions.stem: Spiculated RBCs with evenly spaced spikes are called:
questions.solutionHtml:
Echinocytes
  • Echinocytes are erythrocytes that have lost their disc shape and are covered with 10–30 short blunt spicules of fairly regular form.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 74

Reticulocytes
  • Supravital staining is used for Reticulocytes
  • Reticulocytes are juvenile red cells that contain remnants of ribosomal RNA that was present in larger amounts in the cytoplasm of the nucleated precursors from which they were derived.
  • Cells staining shades of blue, ‘blue polychromasia’, are unusually young reticulocytes. ‘Blue polychromasia’ is most often seen when there is either an intense erythropoietic drive or when there is extramedullary erythropoiesis, as, for instance, in primary myelofibrosis or carcinomatosis.

Supravital Stains for Reticulocytes:

  1. New methylene blue
  2. Brilliant cresyl blue
  3. Azure B 


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 27, 79, 100

questions.stem: Howel-Jolly bodies may be seen after-
questions.solutionHtml:
Splenectomy

Howell–Jolly Bodies

  • Howell–Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants. They are small, round cytoplasmic inclusions that stain purple on a Romanowsky stain.
  • They are regularly present after splenectomy and when there is splenic atrophy. They may be seen in a small percentage of red cells in pernicious anaemia. Usually, only a few such inclusions are present, but they may be numerous in cases of coeliac disease and in other conditions in which there is splenic atrophy and megaloblastosis.

Photomicrograph of a blood film. Postsplenectomy Shows acanthocytes, a target cell and a Howell-Jolly body




Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 642, Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 77

Megaloblastic anemia

Cabot’s ring (Mitotic spindle remnants) is seen in

  • Megaloblastic anemia
  • Thalassemia
  • Post splenectomy


Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 13th Edition, Page No. 1

questions.stem: ESR is a very critical investigation in the diagnosis of TB. Which of the following is true about ESR in TB?

options.label: C
options.text: ESR is raised because of increased RBC aggregate

options.label: D
options.text: ESR is raised due to decreased RBC size

questions.answerText: ESR is raised because of increased RBC aggregate
questions.solutionHtml:
ESR is raised because of increased RBC aggregate
  • Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
  • In TB, ESR is raised because of increased RBC aggregates.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 96

questions.stem: All are true about polycythemia vera except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased ESR
  • In polycythemia vera, ESR is decreased due to a decrease in rouleaux formation or an increase in the RBC surface area to volume ratio.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 97, Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 624, 625, 662

questions.stem: Which of the following indicates hemolysis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Schistocytes
  • Schistocytes: Fragmentation syndromes including MicroAngiopathic Haemolytic Anaemia (MAHA) and mechanical hemolytic anemia (but note that schistocytes can be due to dyserythropoietic as well as hemolysis).

Photomicrograph of a blood film. Microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia. Shows angular red cell fragments.




Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 650, Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 225

RBCs

Echinocytes are types of RBCs

  • Echinocytes: RBCs with numerous short, regular projections from their surface
  • Echinocytes are seen in uremia, premature infants after exchange transfusion, or as artifacts.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 74

Uremia
  • Crenated cells in renal disease are called Burr cells.


Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 1226

questions.stem: Which of the following proteins binds with free hemoglobin in the plasma:
questions.solutionHtml:
Haptoglobin
  • Haptoglobin binds with free hemoglobin in the plasma
  • Free hemoglobin released from lysed red cells is promptly bound by haptoglobin, producing a complex that is rapidly cleared by mononuclear phagocytes. As serum haptoglobin is depleted, free hemoglobin oxidizes to methemoglobin, which is brown in color.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 637

questions.stem: The best method for hemoglobin estimation is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyanmethaemoglobin method

Best method for hemoglobin estimation is the Cyanmethaemoglobin method

  • Cyanmethemoglobin method is the internationally recommended method for determining the hemoglobin concentration of blood.
  • The basis of the method is the dilution of blood in a solution containing potassium cyanide and potassium ferricyanide, where Hemoglobin is converted to HiCN.
  • The absorbance of the solution is then measured in a spectrometer at a wavelength of 540 nm or a photoelectric colorimeter with a yellow-green filter.


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 20-22

questions.stem: ESR is decreased in all the following conditions except
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple myeloma

Lower ESR:

  • Extreme leukocytosis
  • Polycythemia
  • Spherocytosis, microcytosis, Sickle cells
  • Hyperviscosity
  • Low Protein; fibrinogen, gamma globulins
  • Technical factors; dilution, clotted sample
  • Afibrinogenemia


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 94-97

Multiple myeloma

Increased ESR:

  • Old age
  • Female
  • Pregnancy
  • Anemia
  • Paraprotein (Multiple Myeloma)
  • Hypergammaglobulinemia
  • Macrocytosis
  • Elevated fibrinogen (infection, inflammation, malignancy)


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 94-97

questions.stem: ESR depends on all of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Body mass index
  • ESR depends on Viscosity, Fibrinogen, Rouleaux formation & Verticality of the tube but not on whether the patient is obese (i.e. Body mass index or BMI).


Dacie & Lewis Practical Haematology, 12th Edition, Page No. 94-97

Ascorbic acid
  • The bioavailability of dietary iron is as important as the overall content. The absorption of inorganic iron is influenced by other dietary contents. It is enhanced by ascorbic acid, citric acid, amino acids, and sugars in the diet, and it is inhibited by tannates (found in tea), carbonates, oxalates, and phosphates.

Iron Absorption

Site of iron absorption: duodenum and upper jejunum (proximal small intestine)Q.

Ferrous form (Fe2+) of Iron is absorbed.

Transport of Fe2+ into enterocyte occurs via DMT1Q.
